p4_roadmap_fields.identity: Ketogenic diet, a dietary therapy. Formulation, ratio, course and monitoring are in no record this card reads and none is carried. Not a molecule: no identifier.
p4_roadmap_fields.indication_and_transfer: Target population itself (human WOREE), not a bridge from another disease. Limit: all three reported responders carry splice-region or exon-deletion alleles on both sides; the one missense carrier has no diet entry, so nothing transfers to the reference genotype class (CLAIM 042: T2, not demonstrated).
p4_roadmap_fields.novelty_for_woree: Already used in WOREE (CLAIM 042; earlier reports cited by the same source describe use «with varying degrees of success»). Not a new repurposing idea; the open question is the quality of the existing evidence. No new search was run for this card.
p4_roadmap_fields.known_roads_state: Inconclusive (known-roads note 2.7): the exposed denominator is absent, 'responded' is undefined, and a DEE base-rate comparison spans 0 to 100 per cent. In another report the diet «did not significantly improve seizures and was suspended» in a biallelic-null WOREE patient; tried in three and continued in one in another cohort.
p4_roadmap_fields.path_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE only. Not RECUPERO_PROFONDO: nothing in the source measured the gene.
p4_roadmap_fields.expected_contribution: Symptom (seizure control), to be verified. No compensation, function recovery or protection is claimed. Not disease modification.
p4_roadmap_fields.mechanism: Target, type of action, direction and context all UNKNOWN for WOREE. The metabolic-bypass rationale is a hypothesis with no brain energy measurement behind it in WOREE.
p4_roadmap_fields.sources: Internal, WWOX: CLAIM 042, CLAIM 031, CLAIM 001, known-roads note 2.7, early-benefit note row 14 and 1.4/1.5, R4 note HELD-partial answer for the series. External: none read for this card. The authors of the series hedge and recommend in the same breath: «It may be premature to assert the potential beneficial effects of a ketogenic diet as they need to be evaluated carefully in a larger cohort» and the diet «should be considered»; both halves are theirs.
p4_roadmap_fields.evidence_pro_contra: Pro: three clinician-reported responders in one series. Contra or unknown: no denominator; no count; development unchanged in 5 of 5 columns; two of the three responders had died within roughly two years; the text says two of the five patients were previously published, and Table 1's variant-attribution row makes patients 2 and 4 the candidates (an inference from the table; the source does not name them), so any pooled count across WOREE series may double-count them and must name which individuals it counts; the one missense-allele column carries a second de novo likely-pathogenic variant in another gene (confounder); co-medication during the diet is not reported in the retrieved passages; the Results narratives of the responders were never delivered (8 of the article's chunks held).
p4_roadmap_fields.time_to_access: UNKNOWN. Documented obstacles to administrability were assessed in no record read. CLAIM 042 calls the diet a «clinically available intervention»; that phrase is not an access assessment and not paediatric suitability. Clinical census 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven unfiltered queries on ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 returned no registered WOREE interventional study; the one WOREE record is an observational registry and natural-history study. Its own caution binds this card: «A missing hit does not prove that no study exists.» An NCT number proves neither recruitment nor first dosing. A compassionate-use report elsewhere in the repository is news-level, n = 1, and is not a datum for this card.
p4_roadmap_fields.time_to_benefit: UNKNOWN, separately from access. No latency or duration appears on the delivered surface; the narratives where it would appear are not covered. The shortest sufficient follow-up in the non-WOREE precedents is 12 months for instrument change (R4 note), which is not a WOREE estimate.
p4_roadmap_fields.pharmacology: UNKNOWN. No exposure measure appears in any record read. Not applicable in the drug sense.
p4_roadmap_fields.paediatrics_and_interactions: Paediatric suitability is not presumed: a diet is not safe because it is food (early-benefit note). Adverse effects: UNKNOWN in the records read. Interaction with antiseizure co-medication: UNKNOWN (co-medication not reported in the retrieved passages).
p4_roadmap_fields.verification_scope: Supported by: one uncontrolled case series. Reading audited: the early-benefit reading of the series was blind-audited 2026-10-21 (12 triples: 8 supported, 1 overshoot, 2 undershoot, 1 unverifiable; adverse ones repaired at source). Reproduced: no. Replicated: no. This card: no audit yet, OWED to someone other than its author.
p4_roadmap_fields.question_history: CLAIM 042 (including its revival triggers), CLAIM 031, CLAIM 001, early-benefit note, R4 note HELD-partial row. No hypothesis or run entries beyond these.
p4_roadmap_fields.next_measure: Does the Results narrative of the series give the number of children placed on the diet, a seizure count before and after, the interval to response and the co-medication? Closing that needs a native surface of the article (on the operator's PDF list); no access control is to be circumvented.
p4_roadmap_fields.status: IPOTESI (symptomatic only). Not a recommendation for any child.
p4_roadmap_fields.value_added: Makes four things visible at once that a bare 'three of five improved' hides: the absent denominator, the possibly double-counted published individuals (two of five by the text; which two is an inference from Table 1), the flat developmental row, and the untested reference genotype class.

evaluation_frame.source: repurposing_10h_scientist-d_20261021.md, 'The answer in one page', DESIGN TABLE A and B. INFERENZA built from precedents that are all NOT WWOX EVIDENCE; the manifests of that note were blind-audited on 2026-10-22 (207 of 215 triples supported, eight repaired; the repairs are unaudited).
a_woree_evaluation_would_have_to_measure: a repeated, instrument-matched baseline before any exposure, in a form that can move in a profoundly impaired child (growth-scale or raw-score forms rather than standard scores); no measurement of the scatter of an untreated interval in WOREE is established here (the repository's series have one timepoint per patient; no wider search was run)
a pharmacodynamic anchor: none exists for any WWOX-directed intervention (CLAIM 046), so engagement of the intended target cannot be shown at all
one prespecified endpoint with a rescue or withdrawal rule written before the observation window opens
survival, reported beside whatever endpoint is chosen
seizures only as a separate, declared family: a countable fraction, a diary or agreed reconstruction rule, and the seizure-free stratum reported apart (it is prognostic, not a treatment effect)
and_could_not_claim: disease modification or developmental benefit: the developmental-delay row of the one WOREE series reporting a response is identical in every column and two of the three responders had died
that seizure control protects development (CLAIM 031 forbids counting any symptomatic outcome as disease modification)
benefit from a pharmacodynamic move, a global impression or an own-baseline comparison
any effect smaller than the instrument's own untreated scatter

the word protection: in the human precedents read for this frame none measured the preservation of a function that would otherwise have been lost; the repository's mouse rescue studies are outside this frame and the scope of 'this corpus' is not defined, so no wider negative is established here

must_never: No score, rank, probability or blended index. 'Non-dominated' would be a statement about visible dimensions, never a number.
No dose, route, schedule, course or paediatric suitability. Accessibility of a drug, diet or supplement does not prove paediatric suitability.
A computational prediction is not DATO. No engine was run for this card.
Every adjacent source is labelled NOT WWOX EVIDENCE and is never promoted to WWOX evidence.
A missing hit is not proof of absence.
Symptomatic benefit is not slowing of disease; the word 'protection' is not licensed by any evidence on this card.
Where CLAIM 011 has been narrowed, 'dose-dependent' does not stand.
Nothing here is medical advice; it supports discussion with a treating clinical team and never substitutes for one.

next_step: Qualify provenance and context; specify a proximal functional experiment; apply legend-safety-triage.
